questions: What change is needed in perform.ts to eliminate the last shell dependency?
What test coverage is needed for the perform module?
Does the change introduce any new runtime dependencies?

answers.answer: Replace the copyDirRecursive function body (formerly execSync with xcopy/cp-R) with fs.cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true }), and remove the unused import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'. Add cpSync to the existing node:fs import.
evidence: src/update/perform.ts lines 1-9: execSync import removed, cpSync added to node:fs import
src/update/perform.ts line 34: cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true }) is the sole function body

answers.answer: A new perform.test.ts was created with 4 test cases: (1) getInstallRoot resolves to an existing directory, (2) getInstallRoot returns a path containing package.json, (3) static verification that perform.ts source has no execSync/child_process and does contain cpSync, (4) fs.cpSync recursively copies a nested directory tree with correct content.
evidence: src/update/perform.test.ts: 117 lines, 4 test cases in 3 describe blocks
npm test output: 61 tests, 0 failures, all 4 new perform.test.ts tests pass

answers.answer: No. fs.cpSync is a Node.js built-in from node:fs, available since Node 16.7.0. The project requires Node >=18. Zero runtime dependencies were added. package.json was not modified.
evidence: package.json: no changes; devDependencies only (@types/node, typescript)
All imports in perform.ts and perform.test.ts resolve to node:* built-in modules

statement: Replaced the shell-based copyDirRecursive function in src/update/perform.ts with fs.cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true }), removed the unused node:child_process import, and created src/update/perform.test.ts with 4 test cases. npm run build and npm test (61/61) pass. No new runtime dependencies. No getTarExecutable function was introduced — the in-process extraction in extract.ts already eliminates the external tar dependency.
